---
title: "A Worked Analysis from BOLD to a Group Claim"
subtitle: "Tracing a 12-participant reinforcement-learning cohort from run matrices to population trajectories and PPI"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
num <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
check <- readRDS("worked/checkpoints.rds")
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
blue <- "#245D80"
teal <- "#176E66"
orange <- "#A74D2B"
theme_book <- theme_minimal(base_size=13) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor=element_blank(),legend.position="bottom",
        strip.text=element_text(face="bold"),plot.margin=margin(8,12,8,9))
```

Before examining each step in full detail, it is helpful to watch a single scientific question move through the complete MEDuSA pipeline from raw run matrices to population inference. Suppose our primary question is whether signed **reward prediction error (RPE)** modulates neural activity at feedback onset in a prespecified cortical parcel (`Parcel_A`), and how that effect evolves over the surrounding seconds.

Our teaching dataset simulates 12 participants, each completing three runs of 20 reinforcement-learning trials (`worked/workflow-source.Rmd`). Every trial comprises a visual cue, a variable-duration decision interval equal to reaction time, and brief feedback. Two parcels (`Parcel_A` and `Parcel_B`) contain three voxels each, and RPE modulates feedback activity in both parcels. (If you are starting from raw BIDS/`fMRIPrep` directories on disk, see [Step 0: Task Design and BIDS/fMRIPrep Ingestion](medusa_step0_design_bids/medusa_step0_design_bids.qmd); for a quantitative comparison against canonical GLM, FIR, and LSS beta-series, see [Conceptual foundations §5](foundations.qmd#sec-glm-fir-lss-comparison).) Below, we walk through the five core stages of the analysis in execution order and then illustrate two practical data-support and handoff checks.

## 1. Estimate participant HRFs, deconvolve runs, and align parcel epochs (Steps 1–4)

For each participant, three function calls carry the run-level BOLD matrices and event schedules to a de-mixed, parcel-aggregated trial panel:

```{r participant-example}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
library(medusa)

# Step 1: Cross-fit HRFs on non-target runs and estimate own-run AR(p) noise
hrf_fit <- estimate_crossrun_hrf(
  bold, events, tr, candidates, amplitude_model = "trial",
  noise_model = "ar1", evidence = "calibrated"
)

# Step 2: Reconstruct continuous latent activity on an observation-noise scale
dec <- deconvolve_crossrun_hrf(
  bold, hrf_fit, lambda = .1, scaling = "noise_sd", penalty = "sobolev",
  nuisance_mode = "ignore", observation_mask = "fit"
)

# Steps 3 & 4: Aggregate into parcels, de-mix overlapping events, and propagate SEs
epochs <- decon_epoch_regression(
  dec, covariates, target_condition = "feedback", lags = -2:4,
  parcel_groups = parcel_ids, restore_scale = TRUE,
  demix_within_trial = FALSE, tau2_mode = "marginal", return_panel = TRUE
)
```

*(Here `lambda = 0.1` is fixed to match the teaching vignette; in empirical studies, leaving `lambda = NULL` tunes smoothness automatically across runs.)*

### Following a single trial across Steps 1–4 {#sec-worked-checkpoints}

To make each transformation concrete, follow participant **sim01**, **run1**, feedback trial **8** (row `r check$event_row` of `events$run1`, occurring at `r num(check$onset)` s) in **Parcel A**:

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8.2, fig.height=5.3}
#| label: fig-checkpoint-traces
#| fig-cap: "Top: generating and cross-fitted HRF for Parcel A using realized voxel weights. Middle: centered observed parcel BOLD around Trial 8 feedback. Bottom: restored continuous parcel activity from Step 2. Vertical dotted lines mark feedback onset."
h <- rbind(data.frame(time=check$hrf$time, amplitude=check$hrf$generating, curve="Generating HRF"),
           data.frame(time=check$hrf$time, amplitude=check$hrf$fitted, curve="Selected HRF"))
h <- transform(h, view="Step 1 · HRF (seconds after a unit impulse)")
z <- subset(check$stage12, time >= -9 & time <= 14)
b <- data.frame(time=z$time,amplitude=z$bold,curve="Observed",
                view="Step 2 · Centered BOLD (seconds from feedback)")
a <- data.frame(time=z$time,amplitude=z$recovered,curve="Recovered",
                view="Step 2 · Restored activity (seconds from feedback)")
series <- rbind(h,b,a)
series$view <- factor(series$view, unique(series$view))
reference <- data.frame(time=0,view=levels(series$view)[2:3])
ggplot(series,aes(time,amplitude,color=curve,linetype=curve)) +
  geom_vline(data=reference,aes(xintercept=time),inherit.aes=FALSE,color="#71818D",linetype=3) +
  geom_line(linewidth=.9) + facet_wrap(~view,ncol=1,scales="free") +
  scale_color_manual(values=c("Generating HRF"=orange,"Selected HRF"=blue,Observed="#59636C",Recovered=teal)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values=c("Generating HRF"="dashed","Selected HRF"="solid",Observed="solid",Recovered="solid")) +
  labs(x="Seconds",y="Amplitude",color=NULL,linetype=NULL) + theme_book
```

1. **Step 1 (Cross-run HRF & noise):** Run 1's HRF was trained exclusively on `r paste(check$hrf_training, collapse = ", ")`, recovering the generating vascular peak cleanly (@fig-checkpoint-traces, top) before refitting Run 1's $\text{AR}(p)$ noise parameters.
2. **Step 2 (Continuous deconvolution):** Inverting the sluggish BOLD wave shifts the delayed ~5–6 s hemodynamic deflection back to feedback onset ($0\text{ s}$; @fig-checkpoint-traces, middle vs. bottom).
3. **Steps 3 & 4 (Parcel aggregation, de-mixing, and trial weights):** Combining the three voxels of Parcel A with cross-run precision weights (`r paste(num(check$parcel_weights), collapse = ", ")`), subtracting cue/decision bleed, and inverting target mixing yields the per-lag readouts, propagated measurement SEs (`se_demixed`), and composite cohort precision weights below:

```{r checkpoint-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(check$trial,digits=3,row.names=FALSE,
  col.names=c("Lag (s)","Raw readout","Corrected","Measurement SE","Cohort weight"))
```

## 2. Test the planned onset slope across participants (Step 5: `mixed_by()`)

Stacking `epochs$panel` across all 12 participants and centering RPE within each participant and run (`rpe_within`) prepares the cohort panel. To test the planned feedback-onset association in `Parcel_A` (`evt_time == 0`), we fit a random-slope linear mixed model weighted by `precision_weight_cohort`:

```{r planned-example}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
one <- group_panel[parcel == "Parcel_A" & evt_time == 0]
fit <- mixed_by(
  one, model_formulae = list(
    feedback = decon_demixed ~ rpe_within + (1 + rpe_within || id) + (1 | id:run)
  ),
  weights = "precision_weight_cohort",
  calculate = "parameter_estimates_reml", padjust_by = NULL,
  return_models = TRUE
)
```

Across all `r check$n_trials` trials and `r check$subjects` participants, the estimated population feedback-onset slope is **`r num(check$focal$estimate)`** restored BOLD units per RPE unit (fit status: `r if (check$singular) "singular — inspect variance components" else "nonsingular"`).

## 3. Characterize the full lag trajectory and window contrasts (Step 5: `medusa_multilag_infer()`)

When the scientific question extends across the entire $-2\text{ s}$ to $+4\text{ s}$ peri-event epoch, passing the named `subject_epochs` list to `medusa_multilag_infer()` pools participant lag slopes jointly and constructs a simultaneous 95% confidence band covering all seven lags together (`Max-|T|`):

```{r trajectory-example}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
profile <- medusa_multilag_infer(
  subject_epochs, covariates = "rpe", use_whitened = FALSE,
  trajectory_mode = "none", contrast_source = "unsmoothed",
  tr = tr, n_perm = 1999L, n_boot_latency = 0L, seed = 5420L
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8.2, fig.height=4.4}
#| label: fig-worked-lags
#| fig-cap: "Population RPE slope trajectory around feedback in Parcel A. Orange diamond: true instantaneous feedback effect at lag 0 (zero at non-zero lags). Teal dashed curve: noiseless signal projected through the fitted Step 2–3 operators. Blue curve and ribbon: recovered noisy cohort trajectory and 95% simultaneous Max-|T| band."
ggplot(check$group_curve, aes(lag, estimate)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=conf.low.sim,ymax=conf.high.sim), fill="#BBD5DF", alpha=.75) +
  geom_hline(yintercept=0,linetype="dotted",color="#526876") +
  geom_vline(xintercept=0,linetype="dotted",color="#526876") +
  geom_line(aes(color="Recovered"),linewidth=1) +
  geom_point(aes(color="Recovered"),size=2) +
  geom_line(data=check$projected,aes(color="Projected through fitted operators"),
            linetype="dashed",linewidth=1) +
  geom_point(data=data.frame(lag=0,estimate=check$truth),aes(color="Generating effect at feedback"),
             shape=18,size=3.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values=c(Recovered=blue,"Projected through fitted operators"=teal,
                              "Generating effect at feedback"=orange)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=-2:4) +
  labs(x="Seconds from feedback",y="Population RPE slope",color=NULL) +
  guides(color=guide_legend(nrow=2,byrow=TRUE)) + theme_book
```

Notice why the recovered raw lag curve in @fig-worked-lags spans neighboring lags even though the simulated effect occurs instantaneously at $0\text{ s}$: regularized continuous deconvolution spreads a brief impulse smoothly across adjacent lags (matching the noiseless operator projection, teal dashed line).

### Choice point: Comparing a planned window contrast across trajectory curves {#sec-worked-contrasts}

Suppose we test a planned `late_minus_early` contrast (`[2, 4] s` minus `[0, 1] s`) under `trajectory_mode = "deblur_pspline"`, which sharpens the group curve against the known cross-lag mixing matrix (spectral deblurring) before fitting a penalized spline (P-spline). `contrast_source` lets us choose which curve defines the contrast estimand:

```{r worked-contrasts, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8.2, fig.height=4.3}
#| fig-cap: "Early ([0, 1] s) and late ([2, 4] s) contrast windows evaluated on the raw, spectrally deblurred ('unsmoothed'), and deblurred + P-spline smoothed ('multilag') group curves."
cv <- melt(copy(check$curve_versions),id.vars="lag",variable.name="curve")
windows <- data.frame(left=c(0,2),right=c(1,4))
ggplot(cv,aes(lag,value,color=curve,linetype=curve)) +
  geom_rect(data=windows,aes(xmin=left,xmax=right,ymin=-Inf,ymax=Inf),
            inherit.aes=FALSE,fill="#DCEBE6",alpha=.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept=0,linetype=3,color="#708592") +
  geom_line(linewidth=1) + geom_point(size=2) +
  scale_color_manual(values=c(raw=blue,unsmoothed=teal,multilag=orange)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values=c(raw="solid",unsmoothed="dashed",multilag="dotdash")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=-2:4) +
  labs(x="Seconds from feedback",y="Population RPE slope",color=NULL,linetype=NULL) +
  theme_book
```

```{r worked-contrast-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(check$contrasts,digits=5,row.names=FALSE,
  col.names=c("Contrast source","Late minus early","SE","95% lower","95% upper"))
```

The recommended default, `contrast_source = "unsmoothed"`, evaluates the contrast after spectral deblurring and *before* spline smoothing, sharpening lag resolution without introducing spline curvature shrinkage into linear window averages.

## 4. Test seed-to-target connectivity and PPI (Step 6: `decon_connectivity_repair()`)

Finally, when `Parcel_A` moves to the right-hand side to test whether its coupling with `Parcel_B` changes with RPE (`Parcel_B ~ Parcel_A + rpe + Parcel_A:rpe`), `decon_connectivity_repair(..., shared_error = "auto", method = "mmoms")` uses per-trial `se_demixed^2` and cross-parcel noise correlations to correct predictor measurement error while controlling for the main effect of RPE in both parcels. Because our teaching simulation contains no true PPI modulation, the estimated interaction centers near zero as expected.

## 5. Practical checks: Censoring support and file handoffs

Two quick diagnostic checks illustrate how MEDuSA handles incomplete data and file serialization gracefully.

### Observability gating and available-case lag pooling

If late-run frames more than `r check$edge_cut` s after the final feedback trial are censored (`valid_rows = FALSE`), Step 3 retains `sim01`'s final trial at lag $0\text{ s}$ while marking later lags `Missing` once causal HRF energy falls inside the masked tail. Similarly, if one participant lacks all $+4\text{ s}$ readouts, `medusa_multilag_infer()` retains all 12 participants at lags $-2$ to $+3\text{ s}$ and pools the 11 supported participants at $+4\text{ s}$:

```{r support-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  `Lag (s)`=check$edge$lag,
  `Final trial after mask`=ifelse(is.finite(check$edge$estimate),num(check$edge$estimate),"Missing"),
  `Finite participant slopes after +4 s removal`=check$support$n_subjects,
  check.names=FALSE),row.names=FALSE)
```

### Preserving cross-parcel error metadata across exports {#sec-worked-handoff}

Step 6's `shared_error = "auto"` reads full `$unit_error_cor` matrices when given `subject_epochs`, or falls back to the `$panel$shared_noise_loading` column when given a stacked `data.table` or `.rds`/Parquet file. Stripping `shared_noise_loading` during a compact plain-text export leaves no cross-parcel error metadata, causing `"auto"` to fall back transparently to zero shared error:

```{r ppi-handoff-table, echo=FALSE}
h <- as.data.frame(check$handoff)
h$interval <- sprintf("[%.4f, %.4f]",h$lower,h$upper)
h$median_r <- sprintf("%.4f",h$median_r)
h$estimate <- sprintf("%.5f",h$estimate)
knitr::kable(h[c("input","covariance","median_r","estimate","interval")],
  row.names=FALSE,col.names=c("Input","Covariance used","Median error r","PPI slope","95% interval"))
```
